logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Initiated: 'false'
    DestinationPort: 51204
    Protocol: 'tcp'
  filter_loopback:
    SourceIp:
      - '127.0.0.1'
      - '::1'
  condition: selection and not filter_loopback
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationPort:51204 -@SourceIp:(127.0.0.1 OR ::1) -CIDR(@SourceIp, 127.0.0.0/8) @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| LocalPort=51204
| ConnectionDirection=1
| NOT (RemoteAddressIP4=/^(127\.|::1)/)
| ContextImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, LocalAddressIP4, LocalPort, RemoteAddressIP4, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, action, bytes
| filter dstPort = 51204 and action = "ACCEPT"
| filter not (srcAddr like /^127\./ or srcAddr = "::1")
| stats count(*) as sessions, sum(bytes) as bytes, earliest(@timestamp) as firstSeen by srcAddr, dstAddr
| sort firstSeen desc

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port=51204 AND All_Traffic.transport="tcp" AND All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND NOT (All_Traffic.src IN ("127.0.0.1","::1","0.0.0.0")) AND NOT cidrmatch("127.0.0.0/8", All_Traffic.src) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] runC binary modified outside package manager (CVE-2019-5736 / CVE-2024-21626) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Containers on fire: from container escapes to supply chain attacks
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] TeamPCP Checkmarx KICS supply-chain stealer C2 callback (audit.checkmarx.cx / 94.154.172.43) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Kubernetes API curl/wget with ServiceAccount token from container · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
TeamPCP Checkmarx KICS supply-chain stealer C2 callback (audit.checkmarx.cx / 94.154.172.43) AICommand & Control Medium
Catches the post-compromise C2 beacon from the TeamPCP-poisoned KICS Docker image. Network egress to the hardcoded domain audit.checkmarx.cx or the IP 94.154.172.43 from any host running the tainted KICS scanner container. Rationale: Anchors on the exact IP 94.154.172.43 and FQDN audit.checkmarx.cx pre-extracted from the article — the TeamPCP-controlled C2 the KICS stealer talks to during scanning. High-fidelity because these are not generic infrastructure; only an org talking to Checkmarx KICS would even conceivably resolve audit.checkmarx.cx and that domain isn't on any legitimate Checkmarx documentation page (cross-check vs vendor).
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Checkmarx KICS scanner traffic if the vendor publishes a real audit subdomain (verify with vendor — at time of writing this is not a Checkmarx-controlled host)
  • Threat-intel feed validation/sandbox detonation traffic where the IOC is intentionally resolved
  • Misconfigured DNS resolver intercepting and returning sinkhole/replacement for similarly named domains
  • Penetration testers replaying the TeamPCP IOCs to test SOC coverage
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("threat-intel-validator", "sandbox-detonator")) and not(DeviceName startswith "sec-sandbox")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessSHA256 / InitiatingProcessFileName making the connection — is it a KICS scanner binary (kics, checkmarx-kics) running inside a Docker container? Pivot on DeviceId for the previous 24h and look for the parent docker/kubelet process that pulled the tainted image. 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response, kill the offending process tree, pause / cordon the Kubernetes node, and rotate every secret the scanner had access to (ServiceAccount tokens, kubeconfig, CI credentials, registry pull tokens). 3) Hunt: enumerate every host that pulled checkmarx/kics from Docker Hub in the last 90d (image-pull audit logs), look for the SHA256 IOCs 24680027... and 2a6a35... on disk org-wide, and review egress to 94.154.172.43 across all VPCs / egress firewalls.
let bad_ips = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let bad_domains = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (bad_ips) or RemoteUrl has_any (bad_domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let bad_ips = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let bad_domains = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (bad_ips) or DstHostname has_any (bad_domains) or Url has_any (bad_domains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url
title: TeamPCP Checkmarx KICS Stealer C2 Callback
id: 4c1d6f3a-2b8e-4f0a-9f2d-7a1b6c0e8d11
description: Network connection or DNS resolution to audit.checkmarx.cx or 94.154.172.43, IOCs tied to the TeamPCP Checkmarx KICS Docker Hub supply-chain compromise (Kaspersky Securelist 2026-06-01).
references:
    - https://securelist.com/container-attack-vectors/120010/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
    - attack.command_and_control
    - attack.t1071.001
    - attack.initial_access
    - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: linux
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp: '94.154.172.43'
    selection_dns:
        DestinationHostname|endswith: 'audit.checkmarx.cx'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_dns
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate access to Checkmarx managed audit endpoints if your org subscribes (verify the legitimate FQDN with the vendor)
level: high

(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon OR source:kubernetes.audit) (@network.destination.ip:94.154.172.43 OR @DestinationIp:94.154.172.43 OR @network.destination.name:audit.checkmarx.cx OR @DestinationHostname:audit.checkmarx.cx OR @host:audit.checkmarx.cx)
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="94.154.172.43") OR (#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)audit\.checkmarx\.cx$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, DomainName, RemotePort], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="94.154.172.43" OR All_Traffic.dest="audit.checkmarx.cx" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.audit.checkmarx.cx") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="94.154.172.43" OR All_Traffic.dest="audit.checkmarx.cx" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.audit.checkmarx.cx") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Privileged container launch — docker run --privileged from non-CI parent AIExploitation Medium
Detects docker / podman / nerdctl invocations carrying --privileged when the parent is not a known container runtime or CI runner. Privileged containers disable nearly all isolation primitives (all capabilities granted, full /dev access, no seccomp) and are the most common pre-condition for container escape in the article. Rationale: Anchors on the exact `--privileged` flag and `docker exec` strings quoted as code blocks in the article. The CI-parent exclusion catches the legitimate use cases (buildkitd, gitlab/jenkins/github runners) and keeps the alert focused on interactive-shell or unexpected-parent invocations, which is where supply-chain compromise or insider misuse shows up.
ATT&CKT1611 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Build pipelines for Docker-in-Docker that legitimately require --privileged (e.g. legacy dind GitLab runners) — should be allow-listed by hostname or service account
  • Sysadmin hand-running a privileged container to debug a node (treat as sensitive even when expected)
  • Kubernetes node bootstrap scripts launching system pods with privileged: true (kubelet parent is already excluded)
  • Trivy/Anchore/KICS image-scan runners that mount sockets via --privileged
  • Legitimate one-off recovery/backup containers (e.g. velero restore via dind)
Suppression filter
| where not(DeviceName startswith "ci-runner-") and not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/usr/lib/gitlab-runner/","/var/lib/jenkins/"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: who ran it (AccountName), from what parent (InitiatingProcessFileName), and what image (parse the image arg from ProcessCommandLine). Was the image pulled from a trusted registry in the last hour? Look at preceding `docker pull` events on the same host. 2) Contain: stop the container (`docker stop <id>`), isolate the host if the image is unknown/untrusted, and capture the container filesystem for triage (`docker export`). 3) Hunt: list every other privileged container the same user has launched in the past 30d, search for the image's SHA256 across the fleet, and check for downstream container-escape primitives (writes to /sys/fs/cgroup/.../release_agent, /proc/self/exe modifications, host mounts of /).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("docker","podman","nerdctl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--privileged"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (" run "," create "," exec ")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("containerd-shim","buildkitd","kubelet","Runner.Listener","gitlab-runner","jenkins","github-runner"))
| where not(InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("jenkins","gitlab-runner","github-runner","buildkite-agent"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("docker","podman","nerdctl") or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b(docker|podman|nerdctl)\b"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--privileged"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (" run "," create "," exec ")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("containerd-shim","buildkitd","kubelet","Runner.Listener","gitlab-runner","jenkins","github-runner"))
| where not(ActorUsername in~ ("jenkins","gitlab-runner","github-runner","buildkite-agent"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Privileged Container Launch via docker/podman --privileged
id: 9d7e1b22-3f64-4e8a-b1c0-5a2f8d4e9c33
description: docker / podman / nerdctl invoked with --privileged plus run|create|exec, indicating a fully privileged container that disables Linux isolation primitives and enables container-escape primitives discussed in the Kaspersky container attack-vectors article.
references:
    - https://securelist.com/container-attack-vectors/120010/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
    - attack.privilege_escalation
    - attack.t1611
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1610
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
detection:
    selection_bin:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/docker'
            - '/podman'
            - '/nerdctl'
    selection_flag:
        CommandLine|contains: '--privileged'
    selection_verb:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - ' run '
            - ' create '
            - ' exec '
    filter_parent:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - 'containerd-shim'
            - 'buildkitd'
            - 'kubelet'
            - 'gitlab-runner'
            - 'jenkins'
            - 'github-runner'
    condition: selection_bin and selection_flag and selection_verb and not filter_parent
falsepositives:
    - Hand-debugging by sysadmins (treat as a sensitive event regardless)
    - Legacy build pipelines that genuinely require --privileged (should be allow-listed by hostname/user)
level: medium

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.executable.path:(*/docker OR */podman OR */nerdctl)) @process.command_line:*--privileged* @process.command_line:(*" run "* OR *" create "* OR *" exec "*) -@process.parent.executable.path:(*/containerd-shim* OR */buildkitd OR */kubelet OR */gitlab-runner OR */jenkins) -@user.name:(jenkins OR gitlab-runner OR github-runner)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(docker|podman|nerdctl)$/i CommandLine=/--privileged/i CommandLine=/\s(run|create|exec)\s/i
| NOT (ParentBaseFileName=/^(containerd-shim.*|buildkitd|kubelet|Runner\.Listener|gitlab-runner|jenkins|github-runner)$/i)
| NOT (UserName=/^(jenkins|gitlab-runner|github-runner|buildkite-agent)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="docker" OR Processes.process_name="podman" OR Processes.process_name="nerdctl") Processes.process="*--privileged*" (Processes.process="* run *" OR Processes.process="* create *") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT (parent_process_name IN ("containerd-shim","containerd-shim-runc-v2","buildkitd","kubelet","Runner.Listener","runner","gitlab-runner","jenkins","agent","bash") AND user IN ("jenkins","gitlab-runner","github-runner"))
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="docker" OR Processes.process_name="podman" OR Processes.process_name="nerdctl") Processes.process="*--privileged*" (Processes.process="* run *" OR Processes.process="* create *") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT (parent_process_name IN ("containerd-shim","containerd-shim-runc-v2","buildkitd","kubelet","Runner.Listener","runner","gitlab-runner","jenkins","agent","bash") AND user IN ("jenkins","gitlab-runner","github-runner"))
Container escape via cgroups release_agent write (CVE-2022-0492) AIExploitation High
Detects file writes to a release_agent path under /sys/fs/cgroup — the exact primitive abused by CVE-2022-0492 to escape a container and execute arbitrary commands on the host. Pairs the write with the canonical follow-up notify_on_release setting. Rationale: CVE-2022-0492 is explicitly called out in the article as a container-escape vulnerability whose root cause is improper privilege validation on the cgroups release_agent mechanism. The detection anchors on the exact filesystem object the exploit primitive must write to (release_agent + notify_on_release toggle) — there is no benign reason for a containerised workload to touch these files at runtime. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-0492
ATT&CKT1611 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • systemd or lxc-start writing release_agent during legitimate cgroup-v1 setup on older hosts
  • Custom node-bootstrap scripts that explicitly configure cgroup notification (DevOps tooling)
  • Kubernetes node initialization on legacy cgroup-v1 clusters where the kubelet sets release_agent
  • cgroup-tools (cgconfigparser, cgrulesengd) writing release_agent at boot
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemd","lxc-start","cgconfigparser","cgrulesengd","kubelet")) and not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/usr/lib/systemd")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the writing process (InitiatingProcessFileName) — if it's systemd/lxc-start/cgconfigparser/kubelet on a known cgroup-v1 host, it's likely benign; anything else (sh, bash, python, custom binary) is high suspicion. Pull preceding process tree for the last 5 minutes. 2) Contain: snapshot the host, kill the writing process, and if the writer was inside a container, stop and quarantine that container plus its image. Patch the kernel to a CVE-2022-0492-fixed version. 3) Hunt: enumerate child processes spawned shortly after the write (the release_agent fires when the last task in the cgroup exits — expect a short host-side shell shortly after). Search for /tmp/cmd, /tmp/x, or similar attacker payload paths referenced inside the file content if your file-content telemetry captures it.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has "/cgroup/" and (FileName == "release_agent" or FolderPath has "release_agent" or FileName == "notify_on_release")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has "/cgroup/" and (TargetFileName == "release_agent" or TargetFilePath has "release_agent" or TargetFileName == "notify_on_release")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Container Escape via cgroups release_agent Write (CVE-2022-0492)
id: a3e8c5d1-7b22-4f5e-9c11-2d6a8b1e4f72
description: File create/modify on a release_agent or notify_on_release node under /sys/fs/cgroup — the precise primitive CVE-2022-0492 abuses to escape a container by registering an attacker-controlled script that the kernel executes with full host root privileges.
references:
    - https://securelist.com/container-attack-vectors/120010/
    - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-0492
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
    - attack.privilege_escalation
    - attack.t1611
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: linux
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains: '/cgroup/'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '/release_agent'
            - '/notify_on_release'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file
falsepositives:
    - cgroup-v1 daemons (systemd-cgls, lxc start-up scripts) writing release_agent during legitimate cgroup configuration — should be allow-listed by InitiatingProcessFileName
    - Container-runtime initialization on older kernels
level: high

source:linux.auditd (@auditd.type:PATH OR @auditd.type:SYSCALL) (@file.path:(*/cgroup/*/release_agent OR */cgroup/*/notify_on_release) OR @TargetFilename:(*/cgroup/*/release_agent OR */cgroup/*/notify_on_release))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\/cgroup\/.*\/(release_agent|notify_on_release)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/cgroup/*/release_agent" OR Filesystem.file_name="release_agent" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/cgroup/*/notify_on_release") (Filesystem.action="created" OR Filesystem.action="modified" OR Filesystem.action="write") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/cgroup/*/release_agent" OR Filesystem.file_name="release_agent" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/cgroup/*/notify_on_release") (Filesystem.action="created" OR Filesystem.action="modified" OR Filesystem.action="write") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
runC binary modified outside package manager (CVE-2019-5736 / CVE-2024-21626) AIInstallation High
Detects writes to the runC binary on disk by anything other than the legitimate package-manager toolchain. The article calls out CVE-2019-5736 (runC binary overwrite from a compromised container via /proc/self/exe) and CVE-2024-21626 (runC fd handling for host fs access) — both leave the runC executable modified on the node. Rationale: Anchors on the exact runC binary paths and the package-manager exclusion list — CVE-2019-5736 is unique in that successful exploitation requires writing to the host's runC executable from a container context, so any modification of /usr/bin/runc outside the dpkg/yum/snap toolchain is overwhelmingly indicative of either supply-chain compromise or active runC exploit. Also catches the post-exploit cleanup phase of CVE-2024-21626. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-5736 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-21626
ATT&CKT1611 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ansible/Chef/Puppet deploying a new runC version via file copy rather than apt/yum (allow-list by hostname pattern of config-managed nodes)
  • Manual sysadmin install of runc from a tarball (treat as sensitive — should be ticketed)
  • Container-runtime upgrade scripts that fetch runC from GitHub releases and place it directly
  • OS image hot-patching during cluster autoscaler bootstrap
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ansible-playbook","chef-client","puppet-agent","saltstack")) and not(DeviceName startswith "k8s-bootstrap-")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the current SHA256 of the runC binary and compare to the package-manager-supplied hash for the installed runc version (`dpkg -V runc` / `rpm -V runc`). Inspect the InitiatingProcessFileName and its parent tree — was it spawned from a container (containerd-shim ancestry) or from a host shell? 2) Contain: stop the container runtime on the affected node (`systemctl stop containerd docker`), cordon and drain the Kubernetes node, snapshot the host disk, and replace the runC binary from a known-good package. 3) Hunt: search for the same modified runC SHA256 across the fleet (lateral spread), look at every container that ran on the node in the past 24h for a candidate exploit source, and confirm whether CVE-2019-5736 / CVE-2024-21626 affected the kernel/runc version.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath in~ ("/usr/bin/runc","/usr/sbin/runc","/usr/local/bin/runc","/usr/bin/docker-runc","/usr/libexec/docker/docker-runc") or FileName in~ ("runc","docker-runc")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/usr/bin","/usr/sbin","/usr/local/bin","/usr/libexec")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snap","snapd","zypper","containerd"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath in~ ("/usr/bin/runc","/usr/sbin/runc","/usr/local/bin/runc","/usr/bin/docker-runc","/usr/libexec/docker/docker-runc")
| where not(ActingProcessName in~ ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snap","snapd","zypper","containerd"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, EventType, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: runC Binary Modified Outside Package Manager (CVE-2019-5736 / CVE-2024-21626)

description: Write to the runC executable on disk (/usr/bin/runc, /usr/sbin/runc, /usr/local/bin/runc, docker-runc variants) by a process that is not a known package manager. CVE-2019-5736 abuses /proc/self/exe to overwrite the runC binary from a compromised container; CVE-2024-21626 leaves host artefacts after fd-leak escape.

falsepositives:

level: high

source:linux.auditd (@auditd.type:PATH OR @auditd.type:SYSCALL) @file.path:(/usr/bin/runc OR /usr/sbin/runc OR /usr/local/bin/runc OR /usr/bin/docker-runc OR /usr/libexec/docker/docker-runc) -@process.executable.path:(*/dpkg OR */apt OR */apt-get OR */yum OR */dnf OR */rpm OR */snap OR */snapd OR */zypper OR */containerd)

Kubernetes API curl/wget with ServiceAccount token from container AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the article's literal curl POST pattern against the Kubernetes API (`curl -k -X POST https://<kubernetes-url>/api/v1/namespaces/...`) and the canonical ServiceAccount token path. This is exactly the post-compromise behaviour described for the in-container malicious-actions vector — using the mounted /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token to talk to the cluster API. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article's verbatim Table 2 code block (`curl -k -X POST https://<kubernetes-url>/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods -H ...`) plus the canonical SA-token path the article explicitly calls out as automatically mounted and attacker-valuable. curl/wget shouldn't be hitting the API server in healthy pods — legitimate workloads use SDKs / kubectl.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1528 T1613
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • In-cluster controllers/operators that intentionally curl the API server (Prometheus kubernetes-sd, custom Go/Python controllers using plain HTTP) — allow-list by namespace/image
  • init containers that probe API server readiness during pod startup
  • Health-check scripts in legacy pods that wget the apiserver /readyz endpoint
  • Image-scan / compliance tooling (Falco, kube-bench) that exercises the API surface intentionally
  • Cluster-admin debugging from an `nsenter`/`kubectl debug` ephemeral container
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/usr/local/bin/prometheus","/kube-bench","/falco"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full ProcessCommandLine — extract the HTTP verb (POST/GET/DELETE), the targeted resource (pods/secrets/serviceaccounts) and the namespace; correlate with the EKS/GKE/AKS audit log for the matching request on the same Timestamp and identify which ServiceAccount was used. 2) Contain: revoke the ServiceAccount token (`kubectl delete secret <sa-token>` and rotate), evict the offending pod, and block egress from the pod's network namespace. 3) Hunt: from the EKS audit log, list every API action that SA performed in the last 24h (especially `get secrets`, `create pods`, `create rolebindings`), search for outbound exfil from the same pod, and check container image provenance for supply-chain compromise.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","http","httpie")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/api/v1/namespaces","/api/v1/pods","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token","kubernetes.default.svc",":6443/api/",":8443/api/v1/")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kubelet","kubectl","helm","argocd","flux"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("curl","wget","http","httpie")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/api/v1/namespaces","/api/v1/pods","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token","kubernetes.default.svc",":6443/api/",":8443/api/v1/")
| where not(ParentProcessName in~ ("kubelet","kubectl","helm","argocd","flux"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Kubernetes API curl/wget with ServiceAccount Token Path from Container
id: 1f9b0d4e-8a37-4c25-b6e9-3d1a5e7f2c48
description: curl / wget / httpie referencing the Kubernetes API server (/api/v1/namespaces, /api/v1/pods, kubernetes.default.svc, :6443/api) or the canonical ServiceAccount token path. The article quotes verbatim `curl -k -X POST https://<kubernetes-url>/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods -H "..."` as the in-container abuse pattern.
references:
    - https://securelist.com/container-attack-vectors/120010/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
    - attack.credential_access
    - attack.t1552.001
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.discovery
    - attack.t1613
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
detection:
    selection_bin:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/curl'
            - '/wget'
            - '/http'
            - '/httpie'
    selection_kube:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/api/v1/namespaces'
            - '/api/v1/pods'
            - '/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token'
            - 'kubernetes.default.svc'
            - ':6443/api/'
            - ':8443/api/v1/'
    filter_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '/kubelet'
            - '/kubectl'
            - '/helm'
            - '/argocd'
            - '/flux'
    condition: selection_bin and selection_kube and not filter_parent
falsepositives:
    - In-cluster operators that legitimately curl the API server with their SA token (Prometheus k8s-sd, custom controllers) — allow-list by image/namespace
    - Init containers that probe the API server during pod start-up
level: high

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*/curl OR */wget OR */http OR */httpie) @process.command_line:(*"/api/v1/namespaces"* OR *"/api/v1/pods"* OR *"/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"* OR *"kubernetes.default.svc"* OR *":6443/api/"*) -@process.parent.executable.path:(*/kubelet OR */kubectl OR */helm OR */argocd OR */flux)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(curl|wget|http|httpie)$/i CommandLine=/(\/api\/v1\/(namespaces|pods)|\/var\/run\/secrets\/kubernetes\.io\/serviceaccount\/token|kubernetes\.default\.svc|:6443\/api\/|:8443\/api\/v1\/)/i
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(kubelet|kubectl|helm|argocd|flux)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/eks/<cluster-name>/cluster
fields @timestamp, user.username, sourceIPs, verb, requestURI, userAgent, objectRef.resource, objectRef.namespace, responseStatus.code
| filter userAgent like /^(curl|Wget|HTTPie)/i
      and user.username like /system:serviceaccount:/
      and verb in ["create","get","list","patch","delete","watch"]
| sort @timestamp desc
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="curl" OR Processes.process_name="wget" OR Processes.process_name="http" OR Processes.process_name="httpie") (Processes.process="*/api/v1/namespaces*" OR Processes.process="*/api/v1/pods*" OR Processes.process="*/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token*" OR Processes.process="*kubernetes.default.svc*" OR Processes.process="*:6443/api/*" OR Processes.process="*:8443/api/v1/*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search NOT parent_process_name IN ("kubelet","kubectl","helm")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="curl" OR Processes.process_name="wget" OR Processes.process_name="http" OR Processes.process_name="httpie") (Processes.process="*/api/v1/namespaces*" OR Processes.process="*/api/v1/pods*" OR Processes.process="*/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token*" OR Processes.process="*kubernetes.default.svc*" OR Processes.process="*:6443/api/*" OR Processes.process="*:8443/api/v1/*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search NOT parent_process_name IN ("kubelet","kubectl","helm")
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2019-5736", "CVE-2022-0492", "CVE-2024-21626")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2019-5736", "CVE-2022-0492", "CVE-2024-21626")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2019-5736", "CVE-2022-0492", "CVE-2024-21626")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2019-5736", "CVE-2022-0492", "CVE-2024-21626")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or SHA1 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or MD5 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or SHA1 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or MD5 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Miasma supply chain attack: malicious code found in @redhat-cloud-services npm packages

Snyk
2026-06-01 4 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A supply chain worm dubbed Miasma has been found in dozens of @redhat-cloud-services npm releases. The malicious preinstall hook steals credentials, probes cloud identities, and can republish other packages.

ATT&CKT1027 T1190 T1195.002 T1555.003

Detected

Installation
Detected

Command & Control
Likely

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Miasma supply chain attack: malicious code found in @redhat-cloud-services npm p
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious npm packages abuse dependency confusion to profile developer environments

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-05-30 16 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A dependency confusion campaign leveraged 33 malicious npm packages to collect reconnaissance data from developer and build environments. This report details the attack chain, observed tradecraft, and detection opportunities to help organizations identify and disrupt related activity. The post Malicious npm packages abuse dependency confusion to profile developer environments appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

npm install of dependency-confusion scoped packages (moika.tech actor) AIDelivery High
Detects npm/node executing install lifecycle hooks for any of the nine attacker-controlled organizational scopes published by mr.4nd3r50n, ce-rwb, and t-in-one on 2026-05-28/29. The scope strings appear in the resolution command line during npm install, making this a high-fidelity early-stage signal. Rationale: Anchored on the nine attacker-controlled npm scopes named in the article (@cloudplatform-single-spa, @wb-track, @data-science, @ce-rwb, @payments-widget, @travel-autotests, @t-in-one, @capibar.chat, @sber-ecom-core) — these are not real internal namespaces, so any developer-host hit is by definition an unwanted install.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher reproducing the IOC in a sandbox VM that ships logs to production EDR
  • Internal threat-hunter dry-running this query against fictitious package names that happen to share a prefix
  • Legitimate company that genuinely owns one of these scopes on the public registry (none observed for the nine listed scopes)
  • Forensic acquisition tool capturing historical node_modules content with these strings
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$" and DeviceName !has "sandbox" and DeviceName !has "detonation"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the developer/host, capture full process tree (parent of npm), `npm ls` output, the project's package.json and lockfile, and any node_modules/@<scope>/* package.json showing fabricated GitHub Enterprise / Jira URLs. 2) Contain: isolate the device, kill any running node.exe / spawned detached children, delete the cache marker `~/.cache/<scope>_init/`, force-rotate any credentials, npm/GitHub PATs, SSH keys, and cloud tokens reachable from that workstation since the install timestamp. 3) Hunt: query DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to `*.moika.tech`, search the org's private registry / proxy for further dependency-confusion candidates by scope, sweep all dev hosts for the same scope strings in npm/yarn logs and the cache marker file.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "@cloudplatform-single-spa","@wb-track","@data-science/",
    "@ce-rwb","@payments-widget","@travel-autotests",
    "@t-in-one","@capibar.chat","@sber-ecom-core")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "@cloudplatform-single-spa","@wb-track","@data-science/",
    "@ce-rwb","@payments-widget","@travel-autotests",
    "@t-in-one","@capibar.chat","@sber-ecom-core")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\npm.cmd" or NewProcessName endswith "\\npm.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\npx.cmd" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\npm.cmd"
| where CommandLine has_any (
    "@cloudplatform-single-spa","@wb-track","@data-science/",
    "@ce-rwb","@payments-widget","@travel-autotests",
    "@t-in-one","@capibar.chat","@sber-ecom-core")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

C2 callback to moika.tech payload distribution infrastructure AICommand & Control High
Detects outbound HTTPS from any process to oob.moika.tech or the parent moika.tech domain — the dropper fetches its platform-specific payload from https://oob.moika.tech/payload/{win|mac|linux}. Catches the post-install reconnaissance stager regardless of which scope triggered it. Rationale: oob.moika.tech (and the parent moika.tech) is the single C2 endpoint named in the article — every package in the cluster fetches https://oob.moika.tech/payload/<platform>. Domain has no legitimate dev-tooling use and was first seen in this campaign on 2026-05-28.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel team detonating the IOC in a sandbox feeding the same SIEM
  • Researcher manually browsing the C2 from a desktop to confirm takedown
  • Threat-intel feed enrichment service issuing test pulls against the domain
  • DNS sinkhole returning a response that still appears as a query in logs
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot from the connecting host to InitiatingProcessFileName — confirm it's node/npm/npx and capture the project path. Pull the package.json and node_modules tree to identify which malicious scope triggered. 2) Contain: block *.moika.tech at egress (proxy / firewall / SWG), isolate the host, kill the detached child process and clear the temp file written from /payload/<platform>. 3) Hunt: search 30 days of DNS/proxy for any host that resolved moika.tech, search private registry mirror logs for resolutions of the nine actor scopes, and rotate any credentials/tokens accessible to identified developer accounts.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech")
   or RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)moika\.tech/payload/(win|mac|linux)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where DestinationHostName has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech")
         or RequestURL has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech/payload/")
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Name has "moika.tech"
    | project TimeGenerated, ClientIP, Computer, Name, QueryType, Result, ServerIPAddress),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where HttpHostName has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech") or Url has "moika.tech/payload/"
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, HttpHostName, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious postinstall.js dropped under node_modules for actor scopes AIInstallation High
Detects the obfuscated ~7 KB postinstall.js stager being materialised inside node_modules/@<actor-scope>/<pkg>/scripts/postinstall.js. Hunting tier because file-event volume from npm installs is high — the value is in retrospective hunts and forensic timeline reconstruction. Rationale: The article specifies `scripts/postinstall.js` as the obfuscated stager, dropped under each malicious scoped package. Pairing the literal filename with the actor's nine scope strings inside node_modules yields a near-zero-FP file event because no legitimate package would publish under these namespaces.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Forensic image / backup restore writing historical node_modules contents
  • Developer machine restoring from a snapshot taken pre-takedown
  • Malware-analysis VM unzipping the captured package for static review
  • Source-code repo containing an IOC sample file copied from threat-intel report
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !contains "sandbox" and DeviceName !contains "malware" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("forensicimage.exe","7z.exe","winrar.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: SHA256 the file, compare against any IOC bundles MSFT publishes; capture the parent package.json and the npm lockfile to identify which dependency-confusion package was resolved. 2) Contain: isolate the device, delete the package from node_modules and the global npm cache (`~/.npm/_cacache`), force-rotate developer credentials accessible from the host (GitHub PAT, npm token, cloud CLI sessions, SSH keys). 3) Hunt: pivot on `InitiatingProcessAccountName` to find all hosts/projects where that developer ran `npm install` in the last 30 days; check the private registry proxy logs for installs of the same scope from other engineers; sweep CI runners for the same file-event signature.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "postinstall.js"
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
| where FolderPath has_any (
    "@cloudplatform-single-spa","@wb-track","@data-science",
    "@ce-rwb","@payments-widget","@travel-autotests",
    "@t-in-one","@capibar.chat","@sber-ecom-core")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName =~ "postinstall.js"
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (
    "@cloudplatform-single-spa","@wb-track","@data-science",
    "@ce-rwb","@payments-widget","@travel-autotests",
    "@t-in-one","@capibar.chat","@sber-ecom-core")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

node.exe spawns detached child from tmpdir after npm install (moika.tech dropper) AIInstallation Medium
After fetching the platform payload, the obfuscated stager writes it to the OS tmpdir and spawns a detached child. Detects node.exe spawning a process whose image lives in %TEMP% / %TMP% / /tmp where the grandparent chain involves npm — catches stage-2 even if the C2 domain rotates. Rationale: Article describes the deobfuscated execution flow: stager fetches payload from oob.moika.tech, writes it to tmpdir, then spawns a detached child. Constraining node.exe parent + tmpdir child path + correlation with a recent npm install on the same host turns a noisy primitive (node spawning anything) into a campaign-specific signal.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1105 T1564.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Electron/Node-based dev tools writing helper binaries to temp (e.g. esbuild, swc, native module builds)
  • node-gyp compiling native modules under temp during npm install of legitimate packages
  • Webpack/Vite spawning workers from temp directories during build
  • Test runners (jest, mocha) writing temp scripts that node executes
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !has "node-gyp" and FolderPath !has "esbuild" and FolderPath !has "prebuild" and FolderPath !has ".cache\\webpack" and ProcessCommandLine !has "node-gyp" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "node-gyp"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the temp-dir child binary hash, examine for the platform-specific dropper signature (~17 KB JS per article); capture env vars passed (*_RECON_ONLY, *_PKG, *_VER, *_SECRET pattern). Confirm the npm install in the 30-minute window resolved one of the actor scopes. 2) Contain: kill the detached child and parent node, isolate host, delete the dropped binary from tmpdir, clear `~/.cache/<scope>_init/` markers, rotate developer credentials. 3) Hunt: same-host outbound to *.moika.tech, lateral pivot for any other dev who ran npm install in the same project (shared CI runner risk), check whether the RECON_ONLY flag was toggled — if a follow-on payload (>30 KB) was fetched, treat as full compromise rather than recon-only.
let NpmHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd")
        or ProcessCommandLine has "npm install"
    | project DeviceId, NpmTime = Timestamp;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any (
    @"\AppData\Local\Temp\",
    @"\Windows\Temp\",
    "/tmp/",
    "/var/folders/")
| where FileName !in~ ("conhost.exe","node.exe")
| join kind=inner NpmHosts on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (NpmTime .. NpmTime + 30m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          NpmTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, NpmTime)
| order by Timestamp desc
let NpmHosts = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\npm.cmd" or NewProcessName endswith "\\npm.exe" or CommandLine has "npm install"
    | project Computer, NpmTime = TimeGenerated;

| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\node.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any (

| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) @Image:(*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\* OR */tmp/* OR */var/folders/*) -@Image:(*\\conhost.exe OR *\\node.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^node\.exe$/i
| regex("(\\\\Temp\\\\|\\\\AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp\\\\|/tmp/|/var/folders/)", field=ImageFileName)
| NOT (ImageFileName=/\\(conhost|node)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: PATCH /workspaces/{id}/members/{user_id} role-change request AIExploitation High
Hunts the core privilege-escalation primitive in CVE-2026-47416 — an HTTP PATCH against /workspaces/<workspace_id>/members/<user_id> on praisonai-platform <=0.1.2. Because require_workspace_member defaults to min_role='member' and the route never overrides it, any authenticated member can write {"role":"owner"} to any member row. Outside of one-off legitimate owner-driven role tweaks this URL+verb pair is extremely rare, so even URI-only telemetry is high-fidelity for affected deployments. Rationale: Article pinpoints the exact endpoint shape (PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{user_id}) and the route file (api/routes/workspaces.py:115-127). Even without request-body visibility, the verb+path pair is rare enough on praisonai-platform to be high-fidelity; restricting on HTTP 2xx removes 401/403 noise from unaffected versions. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory body and corroborated by independent PraisonAI security coverage on cybersecuritynews.com and Sysdig confirming the platform's pattern of weakly-gated workspace endpoints. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g • https://cybersecuritynews.com/praisonai-vulnerability-exploited/ • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/cve-2026-44338-praisonai-authentication-bypass-in-under-4-hours-and-the-growing-trend-of-rapid-exploitation
ATT&CKT1068 T1190 T1098
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate workspace owner promoting a new admin via the official praisonai-platform UI (verifiable by the actor already holding owner role pre-request)
  • Internal SRE tenant-provisioning script that bootstraps owner accounts on workspace creation
  • Patched 0.1.3+ deployments where the route now enforces min_role='owner' — successful PATCH events are by-design owner-driven
  • Synthetic monitoring / API probe pinging the endpoint as a uptime check
Suppression filter
// Refine by excluding sessions whose caller was already owner (requires JWT decode or join to membership audit):
// | where SrcUsername !in (toscalar(MembershipAuditLog | where Role == "owner" | summarize make_set(UserId)))
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the source IP, JWT subject, and User-Agent from the matching PATCH. Decode the JWT (or query the praisonai member table) to determine the caller's role at PATCH-time AND the target user_id from the URL path — if caller_role!=owner OR caller_id==target_id, treat as confirmed exploitation. 2. Contain: rotate the attacker JWT (revoke session), revert the modified member row to its pre-PATCH role from DB audit, force-rotate all owner credentials in the affected workspace, and block the source IP at the edge. 3. Hunt: enumerate every PATCH /workspaces/*/members/* in the last 30 days, list workspaces where >1 owner was added in a 1h window, and pull GET /auth/me + DELETE /workspaces/* requests from the same session for impact assessment.
// Primary: ASIM web session view (portable across nginx / IIS / App Gateway shippers).
let Lookback = 7d;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
| where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestBodyBytes, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc
