Vulnerable vm2 (<= 3.11.3) present on host — CVE-2026-47210 exposure AIReconnaissance Medium
Inventory hunt for hosts running Node.js applications that bundle a vulnerable vm2 version. Looks for vm2 package directory writes under node_modules and TVM coverage of CVE-2026-47210. Used to scope the blast radius and prioritise patching before any escape detection fires. Rationale: Article names the exact affected package and version range: `npm:vm2 (vuln <= 3.11.3)`. This UC pivots on that fact two ways — TVM lookup by CveId (CVE-2026-47210) for managed inventory, and file-path evidence of node_modules/vm2 for any host the TVM scanner missed (containers, dev workstations, CI runners). Confirmed package + CVE mapping via the GHSA advisory and SCW/SC Media coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6j2x-vhqr-qr7q • https://www.scworld.com/brief/critical-vm2-vulnerability-allows-sandbox-escape-and-arbitrary-code-execution • https://www.isec.news/2026/05/07/vm2-library-hit-by-a-dozen-critical-node-js-sandbox-escape-flaws/
ATT&CKT1592.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dev workstations with vm2 cloned for security research / PoC reproduction (legitimate but should still be patched)
  • Old container images on builder hosts that aren't actively running but show file presence
  • Test fixtures inside other npm packages that vendor vm2 as a transitive dependency for sandbox-testing
  • Backup or restore operations that recreate node_modules trees containing vm2
  • TVM reporting an end-of-life library where the host has the file but the importing application is dead code
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: for each hit, run `npm ls vm2` or grep package-lock.json on the host to confirm the installed version is ≤ 3.11.3 and identify the top-level package that pulled it in (often a transitive). Note whether the host is production, staging, or developer. Step 2 — Contain: open a P2 patch ticket on the owning service team to upgrade to vm2 ≥ 3.11.4 or migrate to isolated-vm; if the service accepts untrusted JavaScript (AI agent code-interpreter, no-code automation, webhook scripting) treat as P1 and consider WAF / input-acceptance pause. Step 3 — Hunt: for any host on this list, run UC-1 retroactively over the last 30 days for node→shell parent-child events, and review outbound destinations from the node process for unexpected egress.
let VulnByTvm = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

let VulnByFile = DeviceFileEvents

    | project Timestamp = LastSeen, DeviceId, DeviceName, Evidence = "node_modules/vm2 package.json present", Paths;
VulnByTvm
| union VulnByFile
| order by Timestamp desc

Node.js process spawning OS shell with enumeration commands — vm2 sandbox escape (CVE-2026-47137) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for node/node.exe directly spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, or bash to execute reconnaissance commands (id, whoami, uname, /etc/passwd reads). This is the post-exploitation signature of a vm2 NodeVM sandbox escape via the nesting:true patch bypass, where attacker JS inside the sandbox reaches child_process.execSync on the host. The PoC in the advisory literally runs `id` via execSync. Rationale: Anchored on the advisory's PoC which spawns `child_process.execSync('id')` from inside the nested NodeVM. Node spawning a system shell is unusual outside of build tooling/CI; pairing the parent=node predicate with classic recon command-line tokens (whoami, id, uname, /etc/passwd) gives a high-fidelity post-exploit signal. CVE-2023-37903 (referenced in advisory) is the original sandbox escape this bypass revives. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8hg8-63c5-gwmx
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.003 T1059.004 T1611
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Node-based CI runners (Jenkins/GitHub Actions agents) shelling out to uname/hostname for environment fingerprinting
  • Electron/Node apps invoking systeminfo or ipconfig for diagnostics dialogs
  • Build scripts using execSync to query git, npm, or system identity at install time
  • DevOps tooling written in Node (PM2, forever, ansible-node) that runs hostname/whoami as part of normal operation
  • VS Code extensions or Node-based dev tools spawning shells for terminal integration
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\.bin\", @"\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\", @"\Jenkins\", @"\actions-runner\", @"\GitHub Desktop\") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("jest", "mocha", "webpack", "npm-cli.js", "yarn.js", "vsce"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the parent node.exe command line — confirm it points at a vm2-using application (look for app entrypoint paths, package.json with vm2 dependency). Check the host's running Node app for known vm2 consumers (sandboxes-as-a-service, code-eval features, low-code platforms). Pull child shell's full command line and any subsequent process tree. Step 2 (contain): If the Node app accepts untrusted code/input, isolate the host and block egress. Snapshot for forensics. Disable the public endpoint of the vm2-using service. Step 3 (hunt): Search 30 days back for the same parent→child pattern on this host and the entire fleet. Check for outbound connections from node.exe to non-application destinations. Pivot on DeviceFileEvents for vm2 package.json writes to map exposure surface (see related UC).

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3) present on host — CVE-2026-47137 exposure surface AIWeaponization High
Hunts for vm2 npm package installs on endpoints/servers — the package's package.json under any node_modules\vm2 path. vm2 was deprecated and ANY version <=3.11.3 is vulnerable to the nesting:true patch bypass that produces full RCE. Use this to inventory exposure for the CVE-2026-47137 mitigation campaign. Rationale: The advisory explicitly names the vulnerable package (npm:vm2 <=3.11.3) and the patched-but-bypassed file (nodevm.js line 263). File-presence telemetry for node_modules/vm2/package.json gives a complete exposure inventory; nodevm.js presence is a precision pivot to the exact vulnerable code path. Triage on file content/version is a follow-up step the SOC runs after the hunt surfaces hosts. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8hg8-63c5-gwmx
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer workstations cloning repositories that legitimately depend on vm2 — true positive but lower urgency than production servers
  • CI build agents installing vm2 as a transitive dependency during npm install
  • Docker image build hosts producing layer caches that include vm2
  • Legacy applications still bundling vm2 with no untrusted-code exposure (e.g. internal-only sandbox use)
  • Security tooling itself (CodeQL, semgrep test fixtures) that vendor vm2 for testing
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): For each hit, read the package.json `version` field to confirm <=3.11.3. Identify the parent application that bundles vm2 — check folder path above node_modules\vm2 for the consuming app's name. Determine whether the app receives untrusted code/input (sandbox-as-a-service, code-runners, formula evaluators are high risk; static internal tooling is lower). Step 2 (contain): For internet-exposed apps using vm2 to sandbox untrusted input, take the endpoint offline or patch immediately — migrate to isolated-vm or Node.js native vm with worker_threads. Step 3 (hunt): Correlate hits with the behavioural UC (node spawning shell). Any host on both lists is likely under active exploitation. Pull npm audit / SBOM data for transitive vm2 dependencies across the fleet.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\vm2\", "/node_modules/vm2/")
| where FileName in~ ("package.json", "nodevm.js", "main.js", "index.js")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen  = max(Timestamp),
            Paths     = make_set(FolderPath, 20),
            Files     = make_set(FileName, 10),
            Writers   = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10)
  by DeviceName
| extend NodeAppHost = iff(array_length(Paths) > 0, true, false)
| order by LastSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\node_modules\\vm2\\", "/node_modules/vm2/")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("package.json", "nodevm.js", "main.js", "index.js")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen  = max(TimeGenerated),
            Paths     = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20),
            Files     = make_set(TargetFileName, 10),
            Writers   = make_set(ActingProcessName, 10)
  by DvcHostname
| order by LastSeen desc

Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3) present on endpoints — CVE-2026-47208 exposure AIWeaponization High
Hunts file-system evidence of the vm2 npm package at vulnerable versions deployed on hosts. The PoC requires the vm2 module to be loaded; any node_modules/vm2/package.json on disk with version <= 3.11.3 is a direct exposure indicator. Use this to bound the vulnerable surface before behavioral hunts. Rationale: Article explicitly names affected package as 'npm:vm2 (vuln <= 3.11.3)'. Detecting node_modules/vm2/package.json on disk is the cleanest exposure indicator before behavioral exploitation. Corroborated against vm2 GitHub advisory and TheHackerNews 2026 vm2 wave write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-qvjj-29qf-hp7p • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/vm2/CVE-2026-24120/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer workstations with legitimate vm2 dependency in package projects
  • CI/CD build agents running npm install for projects pinned to vm2
  • Vendor SaaS agents bundling vm2 in their deployed node_modules
  • Security research VMs intentionally hosting vulnerable vm2 for testing
  • Legacy services awaiting migration to isolated-vm replacement
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("npm.exe","npm-cli.js","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","node.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","ci","update")
// Comment-out the exclusion when hunting active exploitation — npm install is the most likely benign drop source
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm package.json version in the hit path (Read SHA256 vs known-vulnerable hashes; query DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory if Node SCA ingested). Cross-reference host with asset CMDB to determine if it's a dev box, prod service, or unknown. Step 2 — Contain: for prod services, place behind WAF rule blocking known vm2 escape payload patterns and schedule emergency upgrade to isolated-vm; for dev boxes, ticket the owner for package upgrade. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to UC 'node.exe spawning child_process targets' on the same DeviceId for last 14d to catch post-escape activity, and pivot to UC 'sandbox escape PoC strings' to detect attempted exploitation attempts.
// Hunts vm2 package.json drops on disk; pair with DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory if Node modules ingested
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "package.json"
| where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\vm2\" or FolderPath has "/node_modules/vm2/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// ASIM file-event variant — covers vendors shipping file telemetry to Sentinel
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "package.json"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\node_modules\vm2\" or TargetFilePath has "/node_modules/vm2/"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

node.exe spawning child_process targets — vm2 Promise species sandbox escape post-exploitation AIExploitation Medium
Detects the post-escape pattern from CVE-2026-47208 PoC where the attacker uses ex.constructor.constructor('return process')().mainModule.require('child_process').execSync(...) to spawn arbitrary host processes from inside a vm2 sandbox. Filters for node.exe parent spawning shells/cmd/touch/curl/wget without a benign build-tool ancestor. Rationale: PoC ends in 'ex.constructor.constructor("return process")().mainModule.require(\'child_process\').execSync(\'touch pwned\')'. The detectable observable is node.exe parent spawning child_process targets without a benign npm/yarn/electron build-tool ancestor.   • npm/yarn/pnpm postinstall lifecycle scripts spawning cmd or sh

Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the Node script path from process ancestry (look at node.exe's command line for the .js or -e payload) and the immediate parent of node.exe. Determine if the Node service is internet-exposed; check ProcessIntegrityLevel and AccountName for service account context. Step 2 — Contain: if Node service is exposed and child spawned cmd/sh, kill the parent node.exe PID, snapshot for IR, network-isolate the host, and block the source IP at WAF. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to UC 'sandbox escape PoC strings' on the same DeviceId for last 14d to confirm exploitation attempt vs benign behaviour; check DeviceFileEvents for files dropped by the spawned child (the PoC creates 'pwned'); pivot to outbound DeviceNetworkEvents from the node.exe PID for C2 callbacks.

vm2 Promise species sandbox escape PoC fingerprint in scripts/command lines AIWeaponization High
Hunts the specific JavaScript exploitation idiom from CVE-2026-47208 PoC: combinations of Symbol.species class extension of Promise, ex.constructor.constructor('return process')(), and mainModule.require('child_process'). These strings appear in attacker payloads delivered to vm2-using services and in saved exploit files. Rationale: The PoC contains highly distinctive idioms: 'ex.constructor.constructor("return process")()' for breaking out via the prototype chain, 'mainModule.require(\'child_process\')' for arbitrary execution, and 'Symbol.species' class extension of Promise — the actual vulnerable mechanism. These three strings together are extremely rare in benign code. Sigma omitted because the detection chains union/joins across cmdline and file telemetry — single-event shape doesn't fit. Corroborated against the GitHub advisory PoC and GitLab CVE-2026-24120 advisory of the same Promise.species root cause. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-76w7-j9cq-rx2j • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/vm2/CVE-2026-24120/ • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-qvjj-29qf-hp7p
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researchers running vm2 PoC for testing on dedicated VMs
  • Internal red-team exercises validating vm2 patch status
  • Developer education / training materials containing the published PoC
  • Static-analysis or SAST tools scanning for these exact strings (e.g. semgrep rule cache)
  • Blog post authors publishing vm2 escape write-ups whose drafts hit disk

| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sec-research","redteam-","sast-scanner","semgrep-"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("semgrep.exe","sonarqube.exe","snyk.exe","trivy.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: determine if the hit is in a saved .js file (likely targeted exploitation or research) vs a node.exe command line (more likely live exploitation attempt). Pull the full script content from Falcon ScriptControlScanInfo or read the file at FolderPath. Identify whether the host runs an internet-exposed Node service. Step 2 — Contain: if the strings appear in live runtime cmdline on a production Node service, treat as confirmed exploitation — kill node.exe PID, snapshot host, isolate, and look for spawned 'pwned' marker file or other artefacts. If only on disk, quarantine the file and identify how it was delivered (email attachment? git pull? HTTP POST body?). Step 3 — Hunt: correlate with UC 'node.exe spawning child_process targets' on same host ±30 minutes to confirm escape executed; pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound C2 from the node PID; check EmailAttachmentInfo for any .js attachments delivered to the user prior.
// Hunts CVE-2026-47208 PoC fingerprint in node.exe cmdlines AND .js file drops
let poc_strings = dynamic([
    "constructor.constructor(\"return process\")",
    "constructor.constructor('return process')",
    "mainModule.require('child_process')",
    "mainModule.require(\"child_process\")",
    "Symbol.species"
]);
let cmdline_hits =

| order by Timestamp desc

vm2 sandbox-escape PoC strings observed in inbound HTTP request body / WAF AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact JavaScript token sequence from the CVE-2026-47131 PoC (Buffer.call.call/__lookupGetter__/__lookupSetter__ + WebAssembly.compileStreaming + e.constructor.constructor + mainModule.require) in web request URLs and bodies traversing the WAF / reverse proxy. Targets any service that hands user-supplied JS to a vm2 sandbox. Rationale: PoC body in the advisory cites the exact strings Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__"), WebAssembly.compileStreaming(), e.constructor.constructor, and new HostFunction("return process")().mainModule.require("child_process").execSync — those tokens together don't appear in legitimate JSON payloads or REST API traffic. The narrow string set keeps FPs near zero. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v6mx-mf47-r5wg • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-47131
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researchers / red team submitting CVE-2026-47131 PoC payloads to a bug-bounty endpoint
  • Internal vuln-scanner (Nuclei, Burp, ZAP) replaying the public PoC against staging
  • Educational / training apps that legitimately accept sandboxed JavaScript snippets containing __lookupGetter__
  • Codepen-style apps where end users paste arbitrary JS as the product itself
  • Library documentation crawlers indexing the GHSA advisory page
Suppression filter
// Suppress known scanner UAs and bug-bounty staging
| where not (RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nuclei","ZAP/","Burp","sqlmap","WPScan"))
| where not (DestinationHostName has_any ("staging.","-staging","dev.","-dev","bugbounty."))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the request body contains all of {Buffer.call.call, __lookupGetter__/__lookupSetter__, compileStreaming, constructor.constructor} — the full chain, not isolated tokens. Pull the source IP, target endpoint, and verify the receiving app actually uses vm2 (check package-lock.json / Defender DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory for npm:vm2 <= 3.11.3). Step 2 (contain): If vm2 is present and vulnerable, block the source IP at the WAF and snapshot the Node process tree for forensics; isolate the host if a node→shell child was spawned. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the destination service over the last 30 days for the same token set, and search DeviceProcessEvents for node.exe spawning cmd/sh/pwsh on any host running the affected service.

| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wmic.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("echo pwned","child_process","execSync")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

Node.exe spawning OS shell after vm2 sandbox exploitation AIInstallation High
Hunts the post-exploit signature of CVE-2026-47131: a Node.js process spawning cmd/powershell/bash/sh with command lines containing the PoC's distinctive 'echo pwned' marker or child_process.execSync invocations. Node legitimately shells out occasionally for build tooling, so we anchor on the PoC string and the unusual integrity-level / parent-tree combination. Rationale: The PoC ends with execSync("echo pwned", { stdio: "inherit" }) — a near-unique marker — preceded by mainModule.require("child_process"). The node→shell parent-child plus those two string tokens together is article-specific and won't fire on normal Node build steps. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v6mx-mf47-r5wg
ATT&CKT1059 T1068

Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Node-based build tooling (gulp, webpack plugins) that invokes shell hooks containing the literal word 'child_process' in echo'd log messages
  • Test suites for the vm2 fix itself running the PoC against a patched build to assert refusal
  • DevOps shelling out from a Node CI runner with execSync in a logged comment
  • Local developer reproducing the GHSA writeup in a sandbox VM
  • Honeypot / canary nodes deliberately running the PoC for telemetry validation

| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("jest","mocha","pretest","posttest","npm-cli.js install","yarn\\bin"))
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("-build-","-ci-","-runner-","jenkins"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect the node parent process — which package/script invoked it? Pull InitiatingProcessParentFileName and the working directory; confirm vm2 is in the dependency tree (package.json / package-lock.json). Confirm the child shell actually executed (not a string in a log). Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, kill the node PID tree, snapshot memory. If the host is a production app server, fail traffic over to a sibling and preserve disk. Step 3 (hunt): Query the last 30 days for the same parent (node.exe) spawning any shell across the fleet; pull DeviceNetworkEvents from the node PID for outbound connections to non-baseline IPs in the 60 seconds preceding the shell spawn (likely the attacker's IP).
DeviceProcessEvents

Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3) present in Defender software inventory AIWeaponization Medium
Configuration-hygiene hunt that flags any managed host where Defender TVM has indexed an npm vm2 package at version 3.11.3 or earlier, the vulnerable range for CVE-2026-47131. Use this to drive patching outreach before an exploit attempt lands. Rationale: The advisory explicitly states 'Affected packages: npm:vm2 (vuln <= 3.11.3)' and assigns CVE-2026-47131. Defender TVM ingests npm package inventory from app-server hosts and emits a CveId match — the simplest article-specific hunt. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v6mx-mf47-r5wg • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-47131
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendored copies of vm2 inside other npm package node_modules (transitive dep) — counted multiple times per host
  • Developer laptops with global vm2 install used only for local experimentation, not production traffic
  • Container image layers cached on container hosts where the vulnerable vm2 is in a non-running image
  • Honeypot / red-team host that intentionally retains the vulnerable version
  • Archived /backup directories where old node_modules live but no node process actually loads them
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("\\backup\\","\\archive\\","\\.cache\\","\\node_modules\\.bin\\"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): For each hit, confirm whether vm2 is in a *running* service vs an unused dependency — check DeviceProcessEvents for node.exe with cwd containing the vm2 install path. Step 2 (contain): Open a remediation ticket against the application owner with upgrade target 3.11.4+ or migration to isolated-vm / Node.js worker_threads. For internet-facing services, request WAF rule deployment using the UC1 strings as interim mitigation. Step 3 (hunt): Cross-reference DeviceNetworkInfo IsInternetFacing=true against hits to prioritise exposure; check the last 30 days of inbound web requests on those hosts for any UC1 PoC-string matches that may have already landed.
union isfuzzy=true
(
  DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
  | where CveId == "CVE-2026-47131"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
),
(
  DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
  | where SoftwareName has "vm2" and SoftwareVendor has_any ("npm","node","nodejs","openjs")
  | where SoftwareVersion matches regex @"^([0-2]\.|3\.([0-9]|10|11)(\.[0-3])?$)"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion
)
| order by DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-47131")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-47131")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Web service in container spawning interactive shell (Redis/nginx RCE) AIExploitation High
Hunts CVE-2025-49844 (Redis Lua RCE) and CVE-2026-24061 (nginx) post-exploitation pattern: redis-server, nginx, node or java spawning sh/bash/busybox inside a containerised host — the unambiguous fingerprint of RCE landing inside a vulnerable image. Rationale: Article names CVE-2025-49844 (Redis Lua RCE) and CVE-2026-24061 (nginx) as the in-container exploits driving Kinsing/perfctl/Dero/Mirai/Gafgyt staging. Cross-checked against MITRE T1190 page and abuse.ch ThreatFox notes on Kinsing post-exploit shell drop patterns. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/ • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/browse/malware/win.kinsing/
ATT&CKT1190 T1203 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate container init scripts (sh entrypoints) where nginx is actually a child of /sbin/init, not a parent
  • Healthcheck wrappers (e.g. /docker-entrypoint.sh) that legitimately exec curl as a probe — these usually exit fast
  • CI/CD images where nginx-debug-image spawns bash for interactive debugging
  • Sidecar containers like Filebeat invoking sh for log tailing — typically use cat/tail, not curl/wget
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker-entrypoint.sh","healthcheck","livenessProbe")) and not (ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"^[^|]*curl\s+-fsS?\s+https?://localhost")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree for the alerting container; confirm parent PID is the actual service binary and not an init wrapper; check the image SHA against your registry to identify the base image. 2) Contain: pause/kill the container (docker pause / kubectl delete pod), snapshot the volume for forensics, and block egress from the container's subnet at the host firewall. 3) Hunt: pivot on the dropped payload path (/tmp/, /dev/shm/) across every host running the same image, search ContainerRegistryLogs for recent pulls of that image SHA, and check for the Kinsing/perfctl persistence artefacts (cron jobs, ld.so.preload).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("redis-server","nginx","node","java","httpd","apache2","php-fpm")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","busybox","ash","zsh")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","/tmp/","/dev/shm/","chmod +x","base64 -d","bash -i","|sh","|bash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("redis-server","nginx","node","java","httpd","apache2","php-fpm")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/busybox","/ash","/zsh")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","/tmp/","/dev/shm/","chmod +x","base64 -d","bash -i","|sh","|bash")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Container Web Service Spawning Interactive Shell
id: 7e1b8b22-7c11-4f2d-9b40-9a5a3e7e1a01
description: Detects redis-server, nginx, node, java, httpd or apache2 spawning sh/bash with download or staging command-line — classic post-exploit pattern for CVE-2025-49844 / CVE-2026-24061 inside containers.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/container-security-typical-issues/119974/
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1203
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/redis-server'
      - '/nginx'
      - '/node'
      - '/java'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/php-fpm'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/busybox'
      - '/ash'
      - '/zsh'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'curl '
      - 'wget '
      - '/tmp/'
      - '/dev/shm/'
      - 'chmod +x'
      - 'base64 -d'
      - 'bash -i'
      - '|sh'
      - '|bash'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.parent.name:(redis-server OR nginx OR node OR java OR httpd OR apache2 OR php-fpm) OR @ParentImage:(*\\redis-server* OR *\\nginx.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\java.exe)) @process.command_line:(*curl* OR *wget* OR *"/tmp/"* OR *"/dev/shm/"* OR *"chmod +x"* OR *"base64 -d"* OR *"bash -i"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(redis-server|nginx|node|java|httpd|apache2|php-fpm)$/i
| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|busybox|ash|zsh)$/i
| regex("(curl |wget |/tmp/|/dev/shm/|chmod \\+x|base64 -d|bash -i|\\|sh|\\|bash)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("redis-server","nginx","node","java","httpd","apache2") Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","busybox","ash") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(curl|wget|chmod|/tmp/|/dev/shm/|base64|nc |bash -i)") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("redis-server","nginx","node","java","httpd","apache2") Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","busybox","ash") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(curl|wget|chmod|/tmp/|/dev/shm/|base64|nc |bash -i)") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Container privilege escalation via Looney Tunables, PwnKit, sudo chroot AIExploitation High
Detects CVE-2023-4911 (GLIBC_TUNABLES env-var corruption), CVE-2021-4034 (pkexec PwnKit) and CVE-2025-32463 (sudo --chroot/-R) — the exact local-root chain named in the article for Kinsing and perfctl campaigns. Rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2023-4911 (Looney Tunables, Kinsing), CVE-2021-4034 (PwnKit, perfctl) and CVE-2025-32463 (sudo). Detection anchors on the unique exploit signatures — GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc. prefix is the Looney Tunables hallmark, sudo --chroot/-R is CVE-2025-32463-specific. Cross-checked against Qualys advisory for Looney Tunables and the sudo CVE-2025-32463 advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.qualys.com/vulnerabilities-threat-research/2023/10/03/cve-2023-4911-looney-tunables-local-privilege-escalation-in-the-glibcs-ld-so • https://www.stratascale.com/vulnerability-alert-CVE-2025-32463-sudo-chroot • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1180/
ATT&CKT1068 T1548.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate locale/tuning scripts that set GLIBC_TUNABLES for performance (e.g. database tuning runbooks)
  • Authorized chroot-based build/test pipelines invoking sudo --chroot to a sandbox
  • CI agents using pkexec under a service account that isn't root
  • Vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys) running benign exploit probes during scheduled scans
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/opt/vuln-scanner/","qualys-scanner","nessus")) and not (AccountName in~ ("build","jenkins","ci") and ProcessCommandLine has "chroot=/srv/build")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull parent process tree, original logon ID and effective UID transition (auditd USER_ROLE_CHANGE / SYSCALL records); confirm the binary path matches /usr/bin/pkexec or /usr/bin/sudo and not a renamed copy. 2) Contain: kill the offending PID and any descendants, isolate the host from the network, and if it's a container — kill the container and quarantine the image. 3) Hunt: search 24h before and after for child shells from the same logon ID, look for /etc/ld.so.preload writes or new cron entries, and pivot on the inbound RCE that landed the foothold (Phase 1 detection).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.")
    or (FileName =~ "pkexec" and InitiatingProcessAccountName != "root")
    or (FileName =~ "sudo" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--chroot "," -R /","--chroot="," -R="))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine has "GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.")
    or (ActingProcessName endswith "/pkexec" and ActorUsername != "root")
    or (ActingProcessName endswith "/sudo" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--chroot "," -R /","--chroot="," -R="))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Linux Local Privilege Escalation via Looney Tunables, PwnKit or sudo chroot
id: 4d3b9c2e-2f01-4a8e-b6ed-3e6f1e2c2b02
description: Detects the three local-root chains named in the Kaspersky container-security article — CVE-2023-4911 GLIBC_TUNABLES, CVE-2021-4034 pkexec PwnKit, CVE-2025-32463 sudo --chroot/-R.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/container-security-typical-issues/119974/
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-4911
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-4034
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-32463
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1548.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  sel_tunables:
    CommandLine|contains: 'GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.'
  sel_pkexec:
    Image|endswith: '/pkexec'
  sel_sudo:
    Image|endswith: '/sudo'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--chroot '
      - ' -R /'
      - '--chroot='
  condition: sel_tunables or sel_pkexec or sel_sudo
level: high
source:linux.auditd (@process.command_line:*GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.* OR (@process.executable.path:*/pkexec AND -@user.name:root) OR (@process.executable.path:*/sudo AND @process.command_line:(*"--chroot "* OR *" -R /"*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (CommandLine=/GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc\./
   OR (ImageFileName=/\/pkexec$/i AND UserName!="root")
   OR (ImageFileName=/\/sudo$/i AND CommandLine=/(--chroot |\s-R\s+\/|--chroot=)/))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.*","*pkexec*","*sudo --chroot*","*sudo -R *") OR Processes.process_name="pkexec") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.*","*pkexec*","*sudo --chroot*","*sudo -R *") OR Processes.process_name="pkexec") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
perfctl rootkit — /etc/ld.so.preload write or LD_PRELOAD on root daemon AIInstallation High
Hunts the perfctl userland rootkit footprint named in the article: write to /etc/ld.so.preload, or a long-running root daemon launched with LD_PRELOAD pointing at a non-standard library — both are the canonical Linux process-hiding persistence pattern. Rationale: Article explicitly states perfctl 'install a rootkit that hides the presence of perfctl on the system' after CVE-2021-4034. /etc/ld.so.preload and LD_PRELOAD are the canonical Linux userland rootkit primitives. Cross-checked against Aqua Nautilus perfctl write-up and MITRE T1574.006 page. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aquasec.com/blog/perfctl-a-stealthy-malware-targeting-millions-of-linux-servers/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/006/
ATT&CKT1014 T1574.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit profilers/APM tools (Datadog APM, New Relic, Dynatrace) that ship as LD_PRELOAD shims — usually from /opt/datadog-agent/ or /opt/newrelic/
  • Performance debugging via libfaketime / Valgrind / AddressSanitizer in dev environments
  • Snyk / Wiz runtime sensors that inject via LD_PRELOAD
  • Vendor patching tools editing /etc/ld.so.preload during glibc updates
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/opt/datadog-agent/","/opt/newrelic/","/opt/wiz/","/opt/snyk/","dd-trace","libfaketime","valgrind"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read /etc/ld.so.preload contents and identify every library listed; verify SHA256 of each against package-manager hashes (dpkg -V / rpm -V); check which root processes have LD_PRELOAD in /proc/<pid>/environ. 2) Contain: isolate the host, remove unauthorized preload entries, and kill any process running with the unknown LD_PRELOAD; if a container, kill it and quarantine the image. 3) Hunt: search for the dropped library SHA across all hosts, look for the privilege-escalation chain that preceded it (PwnKit/Looney Tunables — UC2), pivot to outbound C2 (UC6).
union
(
  DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where FolderPath =~ "/etc/ld.so.preload" or FileName =~ "ld.so.preload"
  | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
),
(
  DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "LD_PRELOAD="
  | where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/","LD_PRELOAD=/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/"))
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="LD_PRELOAD_exec", FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(
  ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where TargetFilePath =~ "/etc/ld.so.preload"
  | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
),
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "LD_PRELOAD="
  | where not (ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/","LD_PRELOAD=/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/"))
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=DvcHostname, ActorUsername=ActorUsername, EventType="LD_PRELOAD_exec", TargetFilePath="", ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Write to /etc/ld.so.preload or Suspicious LD_PRELOAD on Root Daemon
id: 9c2f54a1-7d6c-4f0d-8a13-2b4f2e9c1d03
description: Detects the perfctl userland rootkit persistence pattern named in Kaspersky's container security analysis — modification of /etc/ld.so.preload or process launched with LD_PRELOAD pointing outside standard library paths.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/container-security-typical-issues/119974/
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1014
  - attack.t1574.006
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename: '/etc/ld.so.preload'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:linux.auditd ((@auditd.type:PATH @file.path:"/etc/ld.so.preload") OR (@auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:*LD_PRELOAD=* -@process.command_line:*LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/* -@process.command_line:*LD_PRELOAD=/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/*))
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\/etc\/ld\.so\.preload$/)
OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/LD_PRELOAD=/ NOT CommandLine=/LD_PRELOAD=\/(usr\/lib|lib\/x86_64-linux-gnu)\//)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="/etc/ld.so.preload" Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","written") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="/etc/ld.so.preload" Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","written") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Container default credential leak — PKP_DB_PASSWORD=changeMePlease and --secret AIWeaponization Medium
Hunts the exact plaintext credential anti-patterns shown in the article's Dockerfile screenshots: PKP_DB_PASSWORD set to changeMePlease (or any default vendor value) baked into image layers, and processes launched with --secret <value> arguments visible in /proc. Rationale: Article's verbatim code blocks include PKP_DB_PASSWORD, changeMePlease and --secret as plaintext-credential examples (Block 1/2/3 in tables). The Phase 3 citation explicitly calls out passwords-on-command-line being visible in /proc. PKP_DB_PASSWORD is the documented OJS/PKP default — confirmed via PKP project docs. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.pkp.sfu.ca/admin-guide/en/deploy-docker • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.003 T1078.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Local dev / lab environments where devs do bake defaults like postgres/postgres
  • One-off bootstrap scripts during fresh-image stand-up (acceptable in test, alert-worthy in prod)
  • HashiCorp Vault / AWS Secrets Manager templating that briefly exposes the value via env injection (parent = vault/aws)
  • kubectl create secret literal commands (parent = kubectl — already excluded)
Suppression filter
and not (DeviceName has_any ("dev-","sandbox-","lab-")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "docker run --rm")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the image SHA and originating registry, pull `docker history` for that image to confirm the credential was baked into a layer (vs runtime-injected); check if the same credential appears across multiple hosts. 2) Contain: rotate the credential immediately at the target system (DB, app, KMS), remove the image from the registry, and block re-pulls of the SHA via admission policy. 3) Hunt: search every host for inbound logons to the downstream service using the leaked credential; check git history for the Dockerfile that introduced it; pivot to UC1 to look for exploitation that may have already used it.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("PKP_DB_PASSWORD=","=changeMePlease"," --secret ","MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=","POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres","REDIS_PASSWORD=redis")
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("vault","sops","kubectl"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PKP_DB_PASSWORD=","=changeMePlease"," --secret ","MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=","POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres","REDIS_PASSWORD=redis")
| where not (ParentProcessName has_any ("vault","sops","kubectl"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Default or Plaintext Credential in Container Process Command-Line
id: b5e2d31a-9c11-43b4-a2f7-3c8e1f4d7e04
description: Detects baked-in default credentials and --secret CLI arguments visible in /proc, as called out in Kaspersky's container security analysis (PKP_DB_PASSWORD=changeMePlease, --secret).
references:
  - https://securelist.com/container-security-typical-issues/119974/
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1552.003
  - attack.t1078.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'PKP_DB_PASSWORD='
      - '=changeMePlease'
      - ' --secret '
      - 'MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD='
      - 'POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres'
      - 'REDIS_PASSWORD=redis'
  filter_vault:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/vault'
      - '/sops'
      - '/kubectl'
  condition: selection and not filter_vault
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*PKP_DB_PASSWORD=* OR *=changeMePlease* OR *" --secret "* OR *MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=* OR *POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres* OR *REDIS_PASSWORD=redis*) -@process.parent.name:(vault OR sops OR kubectl)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| CommandLine=/(PKP_DB_PASSWORD=|=changeMePlease|\s--secret\s|MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=|POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres|REDIS_PASSWORD=redis)/
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(vault|sops|kubectl)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*PKP_DB_PASSWORD=*","*=changeMePlease*","* --secret *","*MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=*","*POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*PKP_DB_PASSWORD=*","*=changeMePlease*","* --secret *","*MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=*","*POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Container-to-container horizontal scan — Dero miner self-propagation AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects compromised containers fanning out to scan adjacent network ranges for additional vulnerable services, the article-described Dero miner self-propagation behaviour. Threshold-based: many unique destinations on a small set of vulnerable-service ports within a short window, sourced from a single container IP. Rationale: Article's Phase 6 citation describes Dero miner self-propagation via infected containers scanning for new targets. Port set chosen for the article-referenced vulnerable services: Redis (6379, CVE-2025-49844), Docker API (2375/2376), nginx-fronted apps (8080/9000), etcd (2379), DBs. cloudwatch_query left empty — container-to-container traffic does not naturally land in CloudWatch CloudTrail/VPC-flow trails in the analyst-pivot shape this UC needs. Cross-checked against Wiz Dero campaign write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/dero-miner-attacks-on-kubernetes-clusters • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/
ATT&CKT1046 T1018
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Kubernetes service-mesh sidecars (Istio, Linkerd) probing pods for readiness/liveness
  • Prometheus blackbox exporter scraping many targets
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Nuclei) running scheduled sweeps
  • Database connection-pool warm-up against a fleet of replicas
  • Container orchestrator (kubelet) health-checking pods
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kubelet","prometheus","blackbox_exporter","istio-proxy","envoy","linkerd-proxy")) and not (DeviceName has_any ("-scanner","vuln-mgmt","qualys-","tenable-"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the source container (LocalIP → pod via kubelet logs or DeviceName); pull its running processes and image SHA; confirm the dest IPs are an actual scan pattern (sequential CIDR walk vs known service set). 2) Contain: pause the source container, snapshot its filesystem and memory, and block egress from its subnet at the host firewall. 3) Hunt: pivot on the image SHA across the fleet to find sibling infections, search outbound DNS for mining-pool stratum domains (UC6), and check for inbound exploit attempts on the listed ports across other hosts.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionAttempt" or ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemotePort in (22, 2375, 2376, 6379, 8080, 9000, 9200, 2379, 5432, 3306)
| where RemoteIPType in ("Private","Public")
| summarize UniqueDests = dcount(RemoteIP), Ports = make_set(RemotePort, 10), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, LocalIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where UniqueDests > 50
| order by UniqueDests desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DstPortNumber in (22, 2375, 2376, 6379, 8080, 9000, 9200, 2379, 5432, 3306)
| summarize UniqueDests = dcount(DstIpAddr), Ports = make_set(DstPortNumber, 10)
          by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where UniqueDests > 50
| order by UniqueDests desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) @network.destination.port:(22 OR 2375 OR 2376 OR 6379 OR 8080 OR 9000 OR 9200 OR 2379 OR 5432 OR 3306)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| RemotePort=22 OR RemotePort=2375 OR RemotePort=2376 OR RemotePort=6379 OR RemotePort=8080 OR RemotePort=9000 OR RemotePort=9200 OR RemotePort=2379 OR RemotePort=5432 OR RemotePort=3306
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemotePort], function=count(field=RemoteAddressIP4, distinct=true, as=UniqueDests))
| UniqueDests > 50
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(All_Traffic.dest) as unique_dests min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port IN (22,2375,2376,6379,8080,9000,9200,2379,5432,3306) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_port _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where unique_dests > 50 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(All_Traffic.dest) as unique_dests min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port IN (22,2375,2376,6379,8080,9000,9200,2379,5432,3306) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_port _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where unique_dests > 50 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Container egress to cryptominer pool / Kinsing C2 AICommand & Control High
Detects post-compromise C2 from containers: outbound connections to Stratum mining-pool ports (3333/4444/5555/7777/14444) or to known Kinsing/perfctl/Dero infrastructure indicators, initiated from a container-resident process (curl/wget/xmrig/perfctl). Rationale: Article ties Kinsing/perfctl/Dero/Mirai/Gafgyt to compromised containers (Phase 8). Stratum port set is the documented mining-pool default for Monero/Dero. Domain indicators cross-checked against abuse.ch ThreatFox Kinsing entries and Aqua Nautilus perfctl/Dero write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/browse/malware/win.kinsing/ • https://www.aquasec.com/blog/perfctl-a-stealthy-malware-targeting-millions-of-linux-servers/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/dero-miner-attacks-on-kubernetes-clusters
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1496
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate mining pools run by research/blockchain teams (rare, but exists)
  • Game-server or NoSQL databases that coincidentally bind to ports 3333/4444 in dev clusters
  • DNS prefetch by browsers in user-namespace containers (Codespaces, Theia)
  • Crypto-trading or wallet sidecars that legitimately resolve pool/exchange domains
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/opt/research/miner/","approved-mining-pool")) and not (DeviceName has_any ("blockchain-research-","crypto-dev-"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the resolving container/pod (LocalIP → orchestrator metadata), the initiating process and full command-line; verify the destination IP against ThreatFox/AlienVault OTX for Kinsing/Dero infrastructure. 2) Contain: kill the container, snapshot its filesystem, block the destination IP and domain at egress; rotate any credentials the container had access to (image-baked creds — UC4). 3) Hunt: correlate with UC1 (web-service-spawning-shell) and UC3 (ld.so.preload) on the same host within 24h; pivot on the image SHA across the fleet; search DNS history org-wide for the same pool domain.
union
(
  DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
  | where RemotePort in (3333, 4444, 5555, 7777, 14444, 14433, 45700)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Signal="stratum_port"
),
(
  DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any ("xmrig","kinsing","perfctl","derohe.org","dero-stratum","minexmr","supportxmr","nanopool","pool.minexmr")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Signal="miner_url"
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
  | where DstPortNumber in (3333, 4444, 5555, 7777, 14444, 14433, 45700)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, Signal="stratum_port"
),
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any ("xmrig","kinsing","perfctl","derohe.org","dero-stratum","minexmr","supportxmr","nanopool")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr="", DstPortNumber=0, Url=DnsQuery, Signal="miner_dns"
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Container Egress to Cryptominer Pool or Kinsing/perfctl C2
id: 6f7e9c41-3b2a-4c98-9d75-1a4f3e2b7c05
description: Detects outbound traffic from containers to Stratum mining-pool ports or to known Kinsing/perfctl/Dero campaign infrastructure indicators named in Kaspersky's analysis.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/container-security-typical-issues/119974/
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/29
tags:

detection:

    DestinationPort:
      - 3333
      - 4444
      - 5555

(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 (RemotePort=3333 OR RemotePort=4444 OR RemotePort=5555 OR RemotePort=7777 OR RemotePort=14444 OR RemotePort=14433 OR RemotePort=45700))
OR (#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(xmrig|kinsing|perfctl|derohe\.org|minexmr|supportxmr|nanopool)/i)

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2023-4911", "CVE-2021-4034", "CVE-2025-49844", "CVE-2026-24061", "CVE-2025-32463", "CVE-2017-9841", "CVE-2023-33246")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2023-4911", "CVE-2021-4034", "CVE-2025-49844", "CVE-2026-24061", "CVE-2025-32463", "CVE-2017-9841", "CVE-2023-33246")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION

RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
